title: Board Games Instructor
description: Job Summary Dinamico Consulting is seeking enthusiastic and responsible Board Games Instructors to support the delivery of our Board Games as a Service (BGaaS) programmes in schools and other learning environments. The successful candidates will facilitate engaging lessons and activities in games such as Chess, Scrabble, Monopoly, and other board games, helping learners develop strategic thinking, problem-solving, communication, concentration, and teamwork skills. This role is suitable for fresh graduates and candidates with 0–2 years of experience who have a passion for working with young people and learning through games. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES - Deliver engaging board games lessons to learners in schools and other approved learning environments. - Teach learners the rules, strategies, and techniques of assigned board games. Facilitate practical games, exercises, challenges, and learning activities. - Support learners at different skill levels and encourage continuous improvement. - Maintain a positive, inclusive, and engaging learning environment. - Monitor learners' participation, progress, and development. - Organize and support internal competitions, tournaments, and board games events. - Encourage learners to develop strategic thinking, problem-solving, concentration, and decision-making skills. - Ensure board games equipment is properly handled, stored, and maintained. - Prepare adequately for each coaching session. - Complete required lesson records and coaching reports. - Communicate relevant learner progress and observations to the programme coordinator. - Work collaboratively with school representatives and other Dinamico Consulting instructors. - Represent Dinamico Consulting professionally when working with partner schools. - Participate in instructor training and professional development activities. - Perform other programme-related duties as assigned.

title: Assembler - SRC Automotive
description:

At SRC, we do things differently. Our associates take pride in their reputation as businesspeople who understand how they impact our bottom line. Their excellent technical skills – accompanied by their role as employee-owners – has become our legacy.

Our Assemblers may work in assembly, testing, packaging, or machining areas of our shop. All work is done according to customer specifications and company processes. Engine knowledge is helpful but not required!

Primary responsibilities include:

  • Works within productions processes to ensure compliance with quality standards; responsible for visual and quantifiable inspection of the final result of their process

We want you!

If you want to think and act like a business owner, SRC Automotive is the place for you! We look for associates who are team players and have great communication skills. Our employee-owner are proactive, uphold commitments and love to continue learning!

Our employee-owners also have:

  • Ability to perform basic math; add and subtract numbers.

What's in it for you?

Employee-owners first, manufacturers second:

If you are interested in joining our team, we would love to hear from you! Please submit an application and our HR team will reach out to you.

title: Set-Up Technician
description:
Special Skills, Experience and Knowledge:
  1. Production and Processing – Knowledge of raw material, production processes, and quality control for maximizing the effective manufacture of product.
  2. Mechanical – Knowledge of machines and tools, including their designs, uses, repair, and maintenance.
  3. Mathematics – Knowledge of arithmetic, algebra, geometry, calculus, statistics and their applications.
  4. Communication – Effectively communicate with others at all levels of the organization both written and audibly to convey necessary information effectively.
  5. Continuous Improvement – Objectively monitoring/assessing performance of yourself, procedures, products, etc., in order to make suggestions or corrective actions that drive continuous improvement.

Key Job Tasks:

  1. Observe machine operation to detect work piece defects or machine malfunctions, adjusting machines as necessary.
  2. Inspect work pieces to verify conformance to specifications using rulers, templates, micrometers, gauges, calipers, or other measuring instruments to meet customer’s specifications.
  3. Perform minor machine maintenance, such as oiling or cleaning machines, dies, or work pieces.
  4. Read blueprints or job orders to determine product specifications, material to be used, and tooling instructions and to plan operational sequences.
  5. Position, adjust, and secure stock material or work pieces against stops, or arbors, or in chucks, fixtures, or automatic feeding mechanisms.
  6. Start machines, monitor their operations, and record operational data.
  7. Test and adjust machine speeds or actions, according to product specifications, using gauges and hand tools.
  8. Instruct other workers in machine set-up and operation.
  9. Record operational data such as dimensional readings, lengths or frequency of strokes, feed rates, and speeds.
  10. Select, install, and adjust alignment of drills, cutters, dies, guides, and holding devices, using templates, measuring instruments, and hand tools.
  11. Set machine stops or guides to specified lengths as indicated by scales, rulers or templates.
  12. Position, align and secure work pieces against fixtures or stop of machine beds or on dies.
  13. Monitor and adjust production processes or equipment for quality and productivity.
  14. Troubleshoot problems with equipment, devices, or products.
  15. Adjust equipment to ensure quality production, using tools such as calipers, micrometers, height gauges, protractors, ring gauges, etc.
  16. Start up and shut down production equipment.
  17. Provide production, progress, or changeover reports to shift supervisors.
  18. Clean Maintain equipment and area around workspace.
  19. Enter, record store or maintain information in written or electronic form.
  20. Perform other tasks as required or directed by supervisor or manager.

title: Director of Early Childhood Programs
description:
The Director of Early Childhood Programs provides strategic and operational leadership for ICAN's portfolio of early childhood services, including, but not limited to, Healthy Families of Oneida, Montgomery, and Schoharie Counties and ICAN Childcare sites in Rome and Syracuse. The Director oversees program quality, regulatory compliance, fiscal performance, workforce development, and continuous quality improvement to ensure the delivery of high-quality, evidence-based, and family-centered services that promote healthy child development and positive family outcomes.

The Director also leads the development and expansion of ICAN's innovative employer-sponsored childcare initiative by building strategic partnerships with employers, community stakeholders, and funders to increase access to high-quality childcare for working families. This position serves as a key ambassador for ICAN's early childhood initiatives, advancing strategic growth through partnership development, public engagement, and collaborative leadership.

Working closely with the Vice President of Family Services, the Director supervises Program Managers and Childcare Center Directors while collaborating across the agency to strengthen systems, support organizational priorities, and advance ICAN's mission.


Duties Responsibilities include the following. Other duties may be assigned.

Strategic Leadership & Program Oversight:

  1. Provide strategic and operational leadership for early childhood programs and departments, ensuring alignment with agency mission, values, strategic priorities, and long-term organizational goals.
  1. Translate agency strategy into integrated program operations, workflows, and implementation priorities across early childhood service areas.
  2. Directly supervise, coach, and support Program Managers and Childcare Center Directors to ensure accountability, strong leadership, quality implementation, staff development, and consistent program performance.
  3. Ensure programs are implemented effectively and achieve intended outcomes while maintaining a commitment to developmentally appropriate, child-centered, and family-focused practices.
  4. Maintain oversight of curriculum implementation, child development practices, family engagement strategies, and continuous quality improvement efforts.
  5. Monitor emerging trends, best practices, and policy changes in early childhood education and child development to inform program innovation and growth.

Community Partnerships & External Relations:

  1. In partnership with the Vice President of Family Services, serve as a liaison with NYS Office of Children and Family Services (OCFS), funders, school districts, early childhood systems partners, and community stakeholders.
  1. Support the development, implementation, and expansion of ICAN’s employer-sponsored childcare model.
  2. Build and maintain strategic partnerships with local employers, business leaders, and community stakeholders to expand access to childcare.
  3. Represent the agency in community coalitions, planning groups, task forces, and collaborative initiatives related to early childhood education and family support.
  4. Support partnerships that strengthen service access, developmental screening, school readiness efforts, family engagement, and coordinated systems of care.
  5. Promote the agency as a trusted leader in early childhood services throughout the community.
  6. Identify opportunities for program expansion, new funding streams, and innovative service delivery models.

Data, Quality Improvement & Compliance:

  1. Develop, monitor, and evaluate program outcomes, quality indicators, contractual deliverables, and key performance indicators (KPIs) across early childhood programs.
  1. Utilize data analytics to identify trends, opportunities, service gaps, and areas for quality improvement.
  2. Maintain oversight of program compliance, licensing standards, accreditation requirements, quality assurance activities, documentation standards, audits, and corrective action planning.
  3. Ensure adherence to all applicable local, state, and federal regulations governing childcare and early childhood programming.
  4. Monitor child, family, and program outcomes to support continuous quality improvement and positive developmental outcomes.
  5. Present program accomplishments, risks, needs, and improvement opportunities to senior leadership through data-informed reporting.

Fiscal Stewardship & Operational Management:

  1. Collaborate with the Vice President of Family Services and Finance Department to develop, monitor, and manage program budgets and fiscal performance.
  1. Monitor program expenditures, staffing patterns, enrollment utilization, funding streams, and resource allocation to support sustainability and quality service delivery.
  2. Participate in budget planning, contract implementation, grant management, and program sustainability efforts.
  3. Make operational and staffing recommendations to maintain fiscal responsibility while achieving programmatic goals.

Workforce Leadership, Human Resources & Culture:

  1. Partner closely with Human Resources and the Vice President of Family Services to support recruitment, onboarding, retention, employee engagement, workforce planning, performance management, and personnel matters.
  1. Foster leadership development among Program Managers and Childcare Center Managers and support succession planning efforts.
  2. Support the recruitment and retention of qualified program staff.
  3. Promote ongoing professional development and continuous learning opportunities for program staff.
  4. Serve as a culture ambassador by proactively supporting, protecting, reinforcing, and modeling agency mission, values, and culture across teams and departments.
  5. Promote a culture of accountability, collaboration, inclusion, professionalism, continuous improvement, and psychological safety.
  6. Participate actively in agency-wide initiatives, strategic planning efforts, and cross-department collaboration to strengthen organizational alignment.

Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Early Childhood, Child Development, Education, or a related field. Master’s degree preferred.
  • At least five years of progressive leadership and management experience.
  • Minimum of 3 years of experience in early childhood education, childcare, family support services, human services, or related settings.
  • Experience with regulatory compliance, quality improvement systems, accreditation standards, childcare licensing, or early childhood systems strongly preferred.
  • Ability to travel frequently across multiple counties/regions.

title: Flight Centre - Travel Consultant - Newmarket, ON
description:
Love travel. Love great conversations. Love the thrill of closing a sale.
Sound like you?

At Flight Centre, our Travel Consultants spend their days having meaningful customer conversations, converting enquiries into bookings, and working toward clear sales targets while earning commission on every sale. You will work in a fast paced, customer facing retail environment where personality, performance, and customer experience all matter.

This role is rewarding, but it’s not easy, especially in your first few months. You will be learning multiple systems, navigating a wide range of products, and managing high volume customer conversations, all while building confidence in a dynamic retail environment.

At Flight Centre, we believe great travel experiences are built through human connection. Technology can book trips, people make them memorable. This isn’t point and click booking. It’s about understanding what really matters to customers, thinking creatively, and bringing genuine value to every conversation.

To learn more about Flight Centre please click HERE

About the opportunity

As a Travel Consultant, you will work full time, on site in one of our retail stores on a rotating roster across a 7 day trade. This is a target driven sales role where success is measured through KPIs, revenue, conversion, and customer satisfaction.

You will take ownership of the customer journey from first enquiry through to booking and follow up, selling complete travel solutions - not just flights.

What You Will Be Doing

  • Convert customer enquiries into confirmed bookings through consultative sales conversations
  • Work toward individual KPIs and sales targets, earning commission on every sale
  • Sell end to end travel solutions including flights, accommodation, tours, cruises, car hire, transfers, and travel insurance
  • Build a loyal base of new and repeat customers - from simple domestic trips to complex international holidays
  • Manage multiple customers and communication channels at once (in-store, phone, email) in a fast-paced retail environment
  • Use booking systems and supplier tools to quote, upsell, book, and follow up accurately and efficiently
  • Other duties and tasks as assigned
  • Contribute to a safe, inclusive, and accessible work environment where all Flighties feel welcomed, respected, and supported to thrive

What Success Looks Like in This Role

  • You enjoy working toward targets and are motivated by results and commission
  • You are confident asking for the booking and closing the sale
  • You balance great customer experience with delivering results
  • You stay organized, resilient, and positive when things get busy

What We’re Looking For

  • Minimum 2 years’ experience in travel sales preferred
  • Experience using Sabre GDS preferred
  • Minimum 2 years’ experience in a customer-facing, target-driven sales role, with a proven track record of meeting or exceeding targets and upselling products or services
  • Strong communication skills and confidence selling in person and over the phone
  • High attention to detail and strong computer skills, with confidence using multiple, complex systems
  • International travel experience
  • High school diploma or higher
  • Availability to work full-time hours, including evenings and weekends

What You’ll Get in Return

  • Competitive base salary plus uncapped commission
  • Clear performance metrics and transparent earning potential
  • Career progression opportunities across Flight Centre’s global brands
  • Industry travel discounts and opportunities to experience the products you sell
  • A performance driven team environment that celebrates results and development

Work Perks! - What’s in it for you:

FCTG is renowned internationally for having amazing perks and an even better culture. We understand that our people are our most valuable asset. It is the passion and dedication of our teams that keep the company on top of the industry ladder. It’s also why we offer some great employee benefits and perks outside of the norm.

  • Have fun: At the heart of everything we do at Flight Centre is a desire to have fun.
  • Reward & Recognition: Celebrate the success of yourself and others at our regular Buzz Nights and at the annual Global Gathering - You'll have to experience it to believe it!
  • Use your smarts: Our people use their quick thinking, expertise, and tenacity to always figure things out.
  • Love for travel: We were founded by people who wanted to travel and want others to do the same. That passion is something you can’t miss in our people or service.
  • Personal connections: We are a big business founded on personal relationships.
  • Diversity, Equity & Inclusion: Commitment to diversity, equity, and inclusion through initiatives like Diversity Day (paid leave to observe a holiday or cultural celebration of your choice) Employee Resource Groups (Racial Equity, Gender Equity, LGBTQ2IA+, Accessibility, Environmental Justice), DEI education initiatives, and equitable practices, including regular equity assessments and inclusive recruitment protocols.
  • A career, not a job: We offer genuine opportunities for people to grow and evolve
  • We back our people all the way: We are strongly committed to supporting every single employee in their professional and personal development.
  • Giving Back: Committed to making a difference through our Corporate Social Responsibility program, which supports nominated charities via volunteering and fundraising, our Office Environmental Program, LEED® Gold-certified office spaces, and 1 paid Volunteer Day per calendar year.

Benefits Include:

  • Generous paid time off policy
  • Travel perks/discounts
  • Health & Wellness Programs and Employee Financial Wellness Services
  • National/International Award Nights and Conferences
  • Group benefits including extended health care, dental and vision, gender affirming care, fertility care
  • Insurance including life, AD&D, critical illness, long term disability
  • Employee Assistance Program
  • RRSP/RPP with matching
  • Tuition Reimbursement Program
  • Employee Share Plan – Ability to purchase company stock on Australian Stock Exchange with partial company match, subject to terms and conditions
  • Global career opportunities in a network of brands and businesses

Don’t Miss Out! Apply now for one of the best adventures you’ll ever have.


Location – Newmarket, Canada

This posting reflects an active vacancy that we are currently seeking to fill.

For this position, we anticipate offering an annual salary of $45,000 plus commission/incentive earnings based on achievable targets. The salary is dependent on relevant factors, including experience, geographic location, and job requirements. On target earnings average range between $45,000 - $68,000. The annual salary range listed represents the total compensation package, excluding benefits.

We welcome applications from candidates with diverse experiences

We thank all candidates for their interest; however, only those selected to continue in the process will be contacted.

Our number one philosophy? Our people. Flight Centre Travel Group’s promise is to provide an environment with equality of respect, dignity and opportunity for all our employees. We value an inclusive and supportive workplace which truly reflects the diversity of our society.

title: Landscape Designer
description:

Full Time Non-Exempt

title: Senior Programme Manager
description:
About Moneybox
At Moneybox, our mission is to give everyone the means to get more out of life. We're guided by our belief that wealth isn't about the money, it's about the means to more - more freedom, opportunities, possibilities, and peace of mind. Moneybox is an award-winning wealth management platform, helping over one and a half million people build wealth throughout their lives, whether they’re saving and investing, buying their first home, or planning for retirement.
Job Brief

Moneybox’s roadmap of product and feature development is delivered as a programme that enables customer, commercial, risk, scalability, and efficiency outcomes. It’s a key lever for achieving Moneybox’s strategic objectives and providing our customers with great experiences and products.

We deliver our roadmap in structured 8-week delivery cycles involving multiple cross-functional Engineering squads (some pooled and some domain-allocated), Product and UX teams attached to products, BAs attached to business systems, and SMEs from functions across the business.

Overall project planning and outcomes are owned by Product and build delivery is owned by Squad Delivery Leads. The Change Team provides centralised programme management, prioritisation structures, trade-off processes, interdependency support, and overarching reporting to enable the Senior Leadership Team to lead and govern the programme as a whole.

This new role is designed to take our programme structures and processes to the next level of maturity and impact, prepare for the pace of change AI will enable, equip SLT with the MI to track benefits and return on investment, and lead orchestration across many teams to help them collectively deliver against the company roadmap. Reporting to the Head of Change, this fast-paced role will influence and partner at all levels of the organisation, flexing between navigating ambiguity, enforcing process consistency, and enabling proportional governance outcomes.

Responsibilities

  • Owns the programme management office across the Roadmap, enabling Engineering, Product, Change, UX, and wider business teams to improve delivery reliability, mitigate risks, and increase our governance

  • Responsibility for the planning, reporting and escalation frameworks used by project teams, empowering Engineering and Product teams

  • Coaches Engineering and project teams in both planning and delivery frameworks as well as on individual project-specific delivery challenges, supporting them through plan reviews, implementing mitigations, and governing changes

  • Manages programme-level planning and escalations to SLT and ExCo, drawing on inputs from Engineering and project teams, including facilitating trade-off discussions, enabling efficient decision making, and providing clear and impactful executive reporting

  • Responsible for risk and dependency mapping across the programme, identifying cross-squad and cross-project dependencies before they block progress and ensuring they are surfaced, owned, and tracked appropriately

  • Matures the roadmap metrics framework by securing agreement to improved MI, data-driven prioritisation and trade-off decisions, and building out a view of benefits realisation and programme ROI

  • Drives cross-functional alignment and process maturity, facilitating scope and resource conversations across Product, Engineering, and other contributing functions.

What we are looking for

  • A significant amount of experience under your belt - you've done this before and don't need much ramp-up time. This likely looks like 5+ years as a Programme Manager and 10+ years overall in change, transformation, data, AI, or engineering delivery managing complex programmes of activity across multiple teams in a fast-paced environment

  • An autonomous, confident, self-starter who gets stuck in fast: you can walk into an unfamiliar environment, work out what matters, and start moving without waiting to be told

  • Genuinely comfortable working in the grey - where the requirement, the owner, or the "right" process isn't yet defined - rather than needing a mapped-out playbook

  • Excellent judgement about what to escalate, when, and to whom - you know the difference between a decision you can make yourself and one that needs appropriate visibility and governance

  • More energised by maturing processes in a scale-up at scale-up pace and ambiguity than by operating in an established environment of a large bank or institution. You'll thrive here if you've built things before, not just followed a framework

  • Someone who can operate with minimal day to day supervision, at pace, and still keep the right people informed

  • You can take vague direction and turn it into concrete outcomes. You break large problems into smaller, logical issues that can be solved in turn, and you can explain your thinking and process clearly enough that others can follow it, challenge it, and build on it

  • We aren’t expecting you to be a software engineer, but you must hold your own in a room of Tech Leads, Product Leads, and business and engineering architects. You must understand software development concepts and have experience in the good and the bad of software project delivery.

  • Deep experience running structured, time-boxed delivery models. We are not looking for a methodology enthusiast: we want someone with a broad kit bag of agile, waterfall, and delivery techniques who draws on whichever fits the problem at hand.

  • Advanced proficiency with project management tooling (Jira, Linear, Asana, etc.) and a proven ability to build clean, scannable reporting. Financially literate: comfortable owning the data behind delivery tracking, capacity planning, and spend.

title: Check In Representative
description:
SUMMARY

Ability to multitask in a fast-paced environment with excellent communication skills. Team members must be patient, upbeat, friendly, and able to work well in a team environment. Check-In answers incoming calls, schedules appointments, or directs callers to appropriate departments while interviewing new patients, verifying demographics and insurance, and inputting information into appropriate systems by performing the following duties.


ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Checks in patients for exams as they arrive which entails verifying information from the patient such as DOB, insurance, and that the exam ordered matches the physician order. The staff enters information into Radiology Information System (RIS) system and works from a number of software systems. This staff member will also scan in necessary documents in the patient’s record.
  • Assist patients with obtaining medical records while complying with HIPAA.
  • Helps the patient when necessary to complete kiosk questions and other forms necessary for their appointment(s).
  • Able to utilize computers efficiently with advanced technology skills and able to adapt easily to change.

title: FIELD OFFICERS
location: Western Area: Western Area Urban, Sierra Leone
description:
Summary:

Reporting directly to the Program Coordinator, the Field Officer acts as the primary liaison between the organization and target communities, educational institutions, and local partners within the operational district. This pivotal role is dedicated to ensuring the safety and well-being of women and girls by facilitating timely, accurate communication among all stakeholders. The incumbent will lead the execution of outreach initiatives, including the coordination of stakeholder meetings, the organization of awareness campaigns, and the monitoring of project activities. Success in this position demands a deep expertise in project lifecycle management, community engagement, and specialized knowledge regarding gender-based violence (GBV), child protection, and safeguarding protocols. The Field Officer must possess the ability to proactively identify and mitigate risks associated with volunteers and interns, ensuring a secure environment while driving the organization's mission forward.

Responsibilities:
  • Lead awareness-raising campaigns on GBV and referral pathways alongside a team of volunteers and interns, ensuring clear communication of Rainbo Centre services.
  • Conduct comprehensive mapping of communities and schools to identify opportunities for outreach and establish new community structures to strengthen GBV referral mechanisms.
  • Facilitate the creation and operation of GBV and adolescent clubs within schools to encourage peer-to-peer dialogue on early warning signs and referral processes.
  • Oversee the recruitment, training, and supervision of volunteers and interns, providing hands-on coaching, mentoring, and assistance in developing work and messaging plans.
  • Organize and conduct regular engagement meetings with stakeholders to educate them on GBV issues, referral pathways, and available support services.
  • Manage media interactions to promote GBV awareness, referral protocols, and the capabilities of the Rainbo Centre.
  • Contribute to the development and execution of annual safeguarding and prevention work plans, ensuring clear definition of responsibilities and activities.
  • Monitor, document, and report on safeguarding and GBV incidents occurring within and around project-targeted schools.
  • Collaborate with the Monitoring and Evaluation unit to gather data related to Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (SEA) and Sexual Harassment (SH) across projects and consultancies.
  • Verify and follow up on safeguarding and GBV cases with partners, including the Family Support Unit and Grievance Redress Mechanism groups.
  • Integrate safeguarding principles into all community and district-level activities and maintain a resource tool for systematic staff education on SEA/SH prevention.
  • Support the Program Coordinator in delivering prevention programs and schedule necessary training sessions for schools, communities, and partners.
  • Identify and partner with local organizations to provide targeted education and prevention initiatives.
  • Provide strategic input on program development, implementation, evaluation, and donor reporting to drive continuous improvement.
  • Plan and execute all project activities in strict adherence to approved work plans, donor standards, and organizational quality benchmarks.
  • Develop activity concept notes and budgets, ensuring efficient fund management, timely requisitions, and accurate liquidations.
  • Partner with the M&E team to implement the MEAL plan, ensuring regular and precise data collection procedures are followed.
  • Represent the organization at external events and meetings as required, and ensure full compliance with all organizational policies regarding fraud, safety, and human resources.
  • Prepare and submit regular weekly and monthly activity reports, plans, and updates on project visits.
  • Contribute to proposal development and maintain an updated project budget tracker aligned with business requirements.

title: Employment Specialist (limited-term)
description:
Are you a person of compassion? An advocate for justice? Someone who stands up for the rights of the vulnerable and speaks out for the marginalized, the exploited and the forgotten? Do you believe in our calling as Christians to welcome the least of these and love our neighbor?

If you answered ‘yes’, to any of the above, World Relief, and millions of people around the world need you.

At this pivotal moment in time, we are rapidly expanding and growing our team to meet the increasing needs of our world. We are looking for people who want to use their gifts and talents to make a real and tangible difference in our world and the lives of the suffering.
If you’re looking for a purpose-driven career in which you can grow your talents, while also standing up for the rights of the vulnerable, we want you to join us today.
ORGANIZATION SUMMARY
World Relief is a global Christian humanitarian organization whose mission is to boldly engage the world’s greatest crises in partnership with the church. The organization was founded in the aftermath of World War II to respond to the urgent humanitarian needs of war-torn Europe. Since then, for 80 years, across 100 countries, World Relief has partnered with local churches and communities to build a world where families thrive and communities flourish.

Today, organizational programming focuses on humanitarian and disaster response, community strengthening and resilience, and refugee & immigrant services and advocacy.

POSITION SUMMARY:
The Employment Specialist will assist refugee clients to prepare for, secure, and retain employment that will make self-sufficiency possible, fulfilling the Match Grant and other program requirements in close collaboration with other employment and casework staff at World Relief.
This is a limited-term position funded through a grant agreement until 5/31/26 and contingent upon funding extension.

ROLE & RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Ensure services, which support and strengthen clients’ motivation and capacities to become self-supporting, are provided in a planned, effective, and timely manner to eligible clients
  • Provide assessment of client’s skills and experience and develop an employment plan with reasonable employment goals and strategies that will lead to employment
  • Make contact with refugees enrolled in the program through office visits and telephone calls (and home visits when necessary) until case closure
  • Document activities through timely case notes which reflect the current status
  • When appropriate, refer clients to other resources including childcare providers, DMV, medical care, job training, transportation information, and other sources and services that will remove identified barriers to employment
  • Provide job counseling and assist clients in developing effective job applications, resumes, and interview techniques
  • Represent World Relief to area employers as a desirable source of workers, acting as liaison between employer and client to ensure good employer relationships
  • Instruct two-hour Job Readiness Class once each week using the prepared curriculum, keep curriculum up to date
  • Enroll clients into relevant programs including completing assessments and developing service plans to track progress of goal achievement
  • Assist clients in accessing community resources Provide orientation on various life skills topics (budgeting, paying rent/utilities, riding the bus, scheduling medical appointments, etc.)
  • Ensure enrollment in ESL courses when applicable
  • Assist clients with appointments, financial literacy, and goal-oriented individualized service plans
  • Ensure security of full-time employment and offer transportation solutions of clients within their first 5 years in the USA
  • Orientation to culture and expectations of work in the US
  • Counseling clients about benefits of early employment
  • Monitor client’s ELT attendance to increase employability
  • Follow up with clients after job placement to address areas of concern and ensure continued employment
  • Participate in the design and execution of programs or courses geared toward client development for increased employability and skills
  • Maintain and complete detailed and accurate records of client files, case notes, and reporting records and submit monthly program reports

JOB REQUIREMENTS:

  • Mature and personal Christian faith
  • Committed to the mission, vision, and values of World Relief
  • Desire to serve and empower the Church to impact vulnerable communities
  • Able to affirm and/or acknowledge World Reliefs Core Beliefs, Statement of Faith, Christian Identity and National Association of Evangelicals' For the Health of The Nation document
  • Computer literate, with proficiency in MS Office (Outlook, Excel, and Word) and internet applications required
  • High School Diploma
  • 2 years’ relevant experience such as direct services and case file maintenance
  • Valid driver’s license, and reliable transportation
  • Prior multicultural experience
  • Experience in a social service setting assisting people in need
  • Demonstrated understanding of case management processes; extremely detail-oriented, excellent time management skills

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Previous case management experience preferred Skill and sensitivity working with people from various backgrounds and beliefs
  • Ability to work with minimum supervision and resolve problems/issues promptly and effectively Ability to work well on a team in a synergistic work environment, a flexible and motivated team player
  • Ability to prioritize, multi-task, and organize in a fast-paced and fluid environment
  • Proficiency in Spanish, Swahili, Dari, Pashto, Burmese, Karen, or Chin is highly desired
World Relief offers a competitive benefits package and employee discount program for full-time, Regular, employees.
World Relief is honored to be recognized with the Gold-level Cigna Healthy Workforce Designation for exceeding the core components of our well-being program including leadership and culture, program foundations and execution, and whole person health.
***
Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.
We are proud to be an EEO/AA employer M/F/D/V. We maintain a drug-free workplace and perform pre-employment substance abuse testing.
For World Relief staff, strong commitment to the mission, vision, and values of World Relief is essential, and Christian faith is a prerequisite for employment, based upon United States federal guidelines provided in Title VII of the Civil Rights Act of 1964.

title: Entertainment Keyholder
description:
WHO WE ARE

Level99 is a sprawling playground designed for adults with over 50 life-sized mini-games where Players dodge axes, crack puzzles, and outsmart real-world challenges. Each game lasts about 1–4 minutes and is built for 2–6 people to play together. One ticket to Level99 unlocks access to all of our games including Challenge Rooms, Player-vs-Player duels, and an art scavenger hunt. We save your progress each time you play so you can earn rewards and climb our coveted leaderboard.

Alongside the games, Level99 offers a full-service bar and award-winning restaurant – featuring scratch-cooking, local craft beers, handmade cocktails, and a variety of event spaces. Level99 has locations in Natick, MA, Providence, RI, Tysons, VA, Disney Springs, FL, and is opening in West Hartford, CT, Paramus, NJ, King of Prussia, PA, and Raleigh, NC. Level99 is backed by Act III Holdings, led by Panera founder Ron Shaich, and we have a talented team that has worked on successful entertainment projects ranging from 5 Wits to Walt Disney Imagineering. Visit for more details.


OVERVIEW

You set the standard for the Level99 experience. As a Keyholder, you’ll lead from the floor, take control of the shift, and step into the Manager on Duty role to keep the Venue running at a high level. You’ll work alongside the Team, make real-time decisions, and ensure every part of the operation stays on track. If you thrive in fast-paced environments, take accountability, and lead with confidence, this role is for you.

RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Act as Manager on Duty, owning shift execution and overall Venue performance
  • Lead the Team through active floor presence, real-time direction, and coaching
  • Maintain control of Guest experience, safety, and policy enforcement across the Venue
  • Oversee staffing, shift flow, and operational execution to ensure a high-quality experience
  • Maintain accountability for cash handling, POS systems, and overall operational accuracy
  • Support event execution and coordinate with internal Teams to ensure smooth delivery

MUST-HAVE SKILLS

  • Friday and weekend availability — a must; flexible schedule including days, nights, and holidays
  • Ability to stand, walk, and stay active for 8+ hour shifts; lift and carry up to 50 lbs
  • Strong verbal communication skills and a natural ability to connect with people
  • Comfortable working under pressure in a fast-paced, ever-changing environment
  • Positive, upbeat, team-first attitude

OTHER DESIRABLE (BUT NOT NECESSARY) SKILLS & EXPERIENCE INCLUDE

  • Minimum 1 year experience working as a leader of people in a high-volume entertainment and/or food & beverage business
  • Minimum 1 year experience as a keyholder in a previous position
  • Relevant Education: B.S. in Hospitality Management, or other related degree
  • CPR/AED/First Aid Certified
While we don’t expect a candidate to have deep experience in all of the above, we’re looking for someone with the passion and capability to learn quickly in the areas that are new!
YOU MIGHT BE A FIT ON THE LEVEL99 TEAM IF YOU…
  • Like to laugh, would be described as a "low maintenance, low drama" person, have a tendency to have a bit of fun while you work
  • Have a high tolerance for ambiguity, like to go fast, and are excited to learn on the job
  • Are just a little bit obsessive about getting the details right the first time
  • Have a high energy personality, the kind of person who is typically smiling, and likes to "get it done now"

title: Director, Government Affairs
company: New York State Energy Research and Development Authority
description:
As a leader in advancing New York’s energy transition, the New York State Energy Research and Development Authority (NYSERDA) is a credible, objective and trusted partner in energy planning and in deploying new innovative technologies to build an affordable, abundant, reliable, and clean energy system. NYSERDA works with stakeholders statewide, including residents, business owners, developers, community leaders, local government officials, universities, utilities, investors, entrepreneurs, and more, to develop, invest, and foster conditions that:

  • Attract the private sector capital investment needed to expand New York’s clean energy economy.
  • Advance solutions for using clean energy at a large-scale in New York.
  • Enable New York’s communities and residents to benefit equitably in the clean energy transition.

Job Overview

The Director, Government Affairs reports directly to the VP for Policy Implementation & Intergovernmental Affairs. The Director oversees a Government Affairs (GA) team charged with interfacing with the Executive Chamber, the State Legislature, municipal officials, other state and local agencies and authorities and other key stakeholders to advance NYSERDA’s Mission Outcomes. This work includes crafting and stewarding a proactive strategy to advance Authority priorities, responding to incoming requests from these entities, informing energy and environmental policy discussions that pertain to NYSERDA, developing responses to enacted legislation, and other engagements as needed.

Primary Responsibilities

  • Lead NYSERDA engagement with local and state elected officials and staff, including leading development and management of engagement with Legislature and Executive Chamber, support NYSERDA Officers, particularly the CEO, at events, and preparation of background and briefing materials for Senior Executives.
  • Coordinate with Vice President, Policy Implementation & Intergovernmental Affairs and Chief of Staff’s office to develop approach to annual Budget/Legislative Session, including preparation for the President and CEO and Officers at legislative hearings and committee meetings, and ongoing engagement with Chamber and Legislative branches. .
  • In close coordination with NYSERDA Officers and Counsel’s office, manage Legislative Departmental submissions and responses to all legislative inquiries, as well as inform NYSERDA management of legislative developments throughout the State Legislature Session.
  • Prepare and conduct briefings for Executive Team, Officers, and CEO on changes to or opportunities to obtain new critical funding or regulatory actions occurring at federal, state and local levels that would impact the Authority’s ability to advance its responsibilities.
  • Manage and oversee all relations with local and state elected officials and their staff.
  • Oversee constituent services and responses.
  • Coordinate with Communications Team, Events Team, Executive Team and program departments to handle and respond to events, press, etc.
  • Attend and represent NYSERDA at events as needed, including speaking at events, conferences, and functions, as needed.
  • Provide excellent verbal and written products, including ability to craft a compelling business/strategic case for Authority outcomes. Write and edit internal and external communications.
  • Serve as an effective coach and leader providing relevant strategic and management guidance to members of the GA Team as well as other departments.
  • Maintain a robust knowledge of local, state, and Federal key issues, priorities, agenda, and sensitivities, particularly as it relates to climate, clean energy, and electrification.
  • Perform all managerial and supervisory responsibilities with respect, fairness, consistency, and inclusion across the workforce.
  • Other duties assigned to support the Authority’s mission and outcomes.

Minimum Qualifications

  • A Bachelor’s degree and 10 years of legislative or relevant experience, including 5 years in supervisory roles
  • In depth knowledge and understanding of legislative processes and actions
  • In-depth understanding of New York State Government and agencies.
  • Genuine passion for advancing sound policy relating to energy and the environment and an interest in developing and supporting a dynamic and talented team.
  • Project management and leadership skills including the ability to work as a team leader and team member, maintain project timelines, budgets, and deliver on commitments.
  • Highest level of communication and interpersonal skills involving the ability to work cross-functionally to understand requirements, present alternatives and recommendations.
  • Self-starter who acts independently, directs one’s own work and can handle diverse tasks quickly and accurately within a high-performance environment.
  • Exceptional manager, coach, mentor, and developer of talent; an ability to lead and develop a team to achieve their potential, innovate and uncover new possibilities, and deliver impactful and relevant outcomes.
  • Demonstrated problem-solving ability, resourcefulness, adaptability, and an instinct for surfacing value and pragmatic solutions.

The Customer Experience Specialist is a temporary position in which the primary responsibility will be assisting customers inquiries while ensuring the highest standards of customer service. none

  • Exceptional written and spoken communication skills

Physical Demands

This job operates in a professional office environment. This role routinely uses standard office equipment such as computers and phones. This position requires a person to have the ability to perform work while stationary for prolonged periods daily. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.


Company Overview

East Fork is located in Asheville, NC , Washington DC, and Brooklyn, NY. At our heart we are makers: we produce every piece of ceramics we sell and source other objects for the home from near and far to offer a meaningful, beautiful, and personal collection of useful objects for the home.


Values at Work

Craft: Craft is not the things we make, it’s the way we make them. It’s the spirit in which we approach our work, to make it nice, to aspire to mastery, and it demonstrates our care about the person who will use the product of our work and how our work impacts their life.


Generosity: We work towards a model of shared prosperity, setting a bigger, more inclusive, more equitable table for everyone we meet - from our employees to the communities in which we live.


Consideration: We approach each other with focus, clarity, and kindness. We think deeply about the outcome and impacts of our actions, on our organization, the individuals within it, our customers, our environment, and our community.


Curiosity: We stay in our beginner's mind, humble, aware of how much we do not know, striving earnestly and open-heartedly towards our shared success.


Diversity, Equity and Inclusion

It is important that all prospective job candidates are aware of our company values and of our commitment to building an inclusive company culture. As a white-led organization, we acknowledge that the realities of white supremacy, hetero/cis-normativity, and patriarchy, work in tandem to oppress both people and planet; and that through our own proximity to power, we have benefitted from systemic inequity. We are committed to confronting and rectifying our privilege in service of co-creating an equitable workplace—a space where people can show up authentically in mind, body, and spirit. We honor the collective sum rather than a monolithic experience to reveal a path of excellency, yours and ours. As we continue to build momentum within our anti-racist work we pledge to be intentional in crafting actions that support diversity, equity and inclusion in our framework, and we invite all East Fork team members to contribute to this goal.

title: Senior AI Engineer, Security Infrastructure
location: Arlington, Virginia, United States; Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, United States; Remote
description:
Company Description

Air is the leader in Enterprise Readiness. Our mission is to establish readiness as a real-time condition that is continuously achieved. Today, a dangerous Readiness Gap exists between what the front line needs and what is delivered. Our AI-native platform, Air Enterprise Readiness, aligns development, production, delivery, and sustainment into one coordinated execution system for government agencies and industrial suppliers. By revealing true capacity, exposing real constraints, coordinating resources, and executing at the speed of operational demands, the front line gets what it needs to succeed.

Job Description

We are seeking an experienced Senior AI Engineer specializing in AI security to join our Agentic AI team as we scale our agentic capabilities across all levels of the U.S. government.
Over the past year, we have seen rapid adoption of our AI agent, Ace. As agents gain access to increasingly powerful tools, data, and workflows, securing these systems presents a fundamentally different set of challenges from securing traditional software.

AI security is not a solved problem. This role sits at the intersection of applied AI research, offensive security, and production systems engineering. You will identify how agentic systems can fail or be exploited, develop new approaches for detecting and mitigating those failures, and build the infrastructure necessary to deploy capable AI agents securely in adversarial environments.

You will work directly with the engineers building our agent runtime, evaluation infrastructure, tools, and production AI systems. The goal is not simply to identify vulnerabilities - it is to turn what we learn into durable security architecture, automated evaluations, and engineering primitives that make our entire AI platform more secure.

This role is a full-time position located out of our office in Pittsburgh, PA or Arlington, VA and Remote for those outside of those cities.

This role may require up to 25% travel

Scope of Responsibilities

  • Research and develop new approaches to AI red teaming, adversarial testing, security evaluation, and robust inference.
  • Threat model agentic AI architectures, identifying trust boundaries, attack surfaces, privileged capabilities, and potential failure modes.
  • Design adversarial evaluations targeting threats such as prompt injection, indirect prompt injection, tool abuse, privilege escalation, data exfiltration, context or memory poisoning, and unintended agent behavior.
  • Build automated security evaluation and regression frameworks that continuously test agents, models, tools, and infrastructure against known and emerging attacks.
  • Translate successful attacks and research findings into production mitigations, architectural improvements, and reusable security controls.
  • Design secure execution environments for AI agents interacting with tools, code, data, and external systems.
  • Build and harden sandboxing and isolation mechanisms for executing agent-generated or otherwise untrusted workloads.
  • Design capability boundaries, permission models, and least-privilege access controls for agent tools and services.
  • Develop scalable AI infrastructure and services supporting secure model inference and agent execution.
  • Own and improve production infrastructure across Kubernetes, AWS, networking, storage, and compute.
  • Implement security controls around identity and access management, secrets, network isolation, containers, and service-to-service communication.
  • Build scalable APIs, internal platform services, and infrastructure tooling that improve developer productivity, system reliability, and security.
  • Improve observability across AI systems through structured logging, metrics, distributed tracing, dashboards, security telemetry, and automated alerting.
  • Investigate complex production and security failures across models, agents, distributed systems, and infrastructure.
  • Optimize performance, latency, and infrastructure cost while maintaining strong reliability and security guarantees.
  • Stay current with emerging attacks against LLMs and agentic systems and rapidly translate relevant research into practical evaluations and defenses.

Qualifications

  • U.S. Citizenship is required
Required Skills:
  • 5+ years of experience building production software, backend infrastructure, distributed systems, security systems, or AI/ML infrastructure.
  • Bachelor's, Master's, or Doctorate in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Cybersecurity, Data Science, or a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience.
  • Demonstrated experience in AI red teaming, adversarial machine learning, offensive security, systems security, or related security research.
  • Experience evaluating AI systems beyond basic direct prompt injection attacks.
  • Strong understanding of how modern LLM and agentic systems operate, including model inference, context management, tool use, retrieval, and multi-step agent execution.
  • Strong intuition for how AI systems can fail when exposed to adversarial users, untrusted data, external tools, and complex production environments.
  • Experience threat modeling complex systems and translating identified risks into concrete engineering controls.
  • Strong programming experience in Python and experience building production-quality software.
  • Experience operating production services on Kubernetes and cloud platforms such as AWS, GCP, or Azure.
  • Strong understanding of networking, distributed systems, containers, service orchestration, and scalable architectures.
  • Experience designing APIs, services, asynchronous systems, and event-driven architectures.
  • Comfortable debugging failures that span application code, AI models, distributed systems, and infrastructure.
  • Able to move between research and engineering: reading new research, developing an attack or defense, validating it experimentally, and turning the result into a production system.
  • Passionate about building secure AI systems and proactively defending against novel attack vectors.

Desired Skills:

  • Experience designing or securing AI agent runtimes and tool-execution environments.
  • Experience building secure code execution sandboxes, container isolation, microVMs, or other mechanisms for running untrusted workloads.
  • Experience with cloud security, infrastructure hardening, IAM, secrets management, network isolation, and zero-trust architectures.
  • Experience with offensive security, penetration testing, vulnerability research, or exploit development.
  • Experience developing automated adversarial evaluations or integrating security evaluations into CI/CD pipelines.
  • Experience with adversarial machine learning, model robustness, or inference-time defenses.
  • Familiarity with AI security frameworks and threat taxonomies such as MITRE ATLAS, OWASP guidance for LLM/GenAI applications, or the NIST AI Risk Management Framework.
  • Experience securing RAG systems, vector stores, model gateways, or other components of modern AI infrastructure.
  • Experience with software supply-chain security and securing model, dependency, and container artifacts.
  • Experience working in government, defense, or other high-security environments.
We firmly believe that past performance is the best indicator of future performance. If you thrive while building solutions to complex problems, are a self-starter, and are passionate about making an impact in global security, we’re eager to hear from you.
Air is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability and protected veterans status or any other characteristic protected by law.

title: Case Planning Program Manager
description:

This position ensures the delivery of high-quality, strength-based, and family-centered preventive services for families referred by OCDFC. title: Emergency Medical Technician
description:
Summary:

The Emergency Medical Technician (EMT) is a vital frontline responder in Barbados’ emergency healthcare system, delivering immediate, life-saving care during medical emergencies. Operating in dynamic environments such as ambulances, accident scenes, and emergency departments, EMTs provide critical initial treatment that can significantly influence patient outcomes. This role demands quick thinking, technical proficiency, and emotional resilience in high-pressure situations. EMTs assess patients using triage protocols, administer basic life support, stabilize acute conditions, and ensure safe transport to medical facilities. Their expertise bridges the gap between the onset of an emergency and definitive medical care, playing a key role in the continuity and effectiveness of emergency medical services across the island. As part of a dedicated healthcare team, EMTs uphold professional standards, ensure regulatory compliance, and contribute to community health resilience.

Responsibilities:

  • Respond rapidly to emergency calls and conduct initial patient assessments using standardized triage protocols.
  • Deliver essential emergency care, including CPR, oxygen administration, wound management, and hemorrhage control.
  • Stabilize patients experiencing trauma, cardiac events, respiratory failure, and other acute medical crises.
  • Operate, inspect, and maintain emergency medical equipment such as AEDs, stretchers, suction units, and monitoring devices.
  • Communicate clearly and compassionately with patients, families, and healthcare professionals to relay critical medical information.
  • Accurately document patient care, interventions, and incident details in official medical records and incident reports.
  • Collaborate effectively with paramedics, nurses, and physicians during patient handoffs at hospitals and clinics.
  • Participate in regular training sessions, emergency drills, and quality improvement programs to maintain readiness and certification.
  • Adhere to all local, national, and international regulations governing emergency medical services in Barbados.

Requirements

Requirements:
  • Current certification as an Emergency Medical Technician (EMT) issued by the Paramedical Council.
  • Valid driver’s license with a clean driving record and proven ability to operate emergency response vehicles safely.
  • Minimum of ${experience_years} years of practical experience in pre-hospital emergency medical care.
  • In-depth knowledge of human anatomy, physiology, and emergency medical protocols.
  • Exceptional communication, interpersonal, and crisis response skills.
  • Proven ability to perform under pressure in fast-paced, unpredictable environments.
  • Physical fitness and strength to lift, carry, and move patients, often in challenging terrain or weather.
  • Flexibility to work rotating shifts, including nights, weekends, and public holidays.
  • Commitment to ongoing professional development, including mandatory continuing education and recertification.

title: Visa Consultant / Agent
description:

Univacity Ltd is looking for an experienced Visa Consultant/Immigration Agent to manage and process visa applications across multiple categories — student, travel, tourism, business, and work visas. title: AI Enablement Specialist
description:
About Fullscript

We’re an industry-leading health technology company on a mission to help people get better. We started in 2011 with one simple idea. Make it easier for practitioners to access the products they trust so they can deliver better care.

That simple idea grew into a platform that powers every part of care. Today, more than 125,000 practitioners use Fullscript for clinical insights, lab interpretations, patient analytics, education, and access to high-quality supplements. Over 10 million patients rely on Fullscript to stay connected to their care plans and follow through on treatment.

We build tools that make care smarter and more human. Tools that save time, simplify decisions, and help practitioners stay closely connected to the people they care for. When everything they need is in one place, they can focus on what matters most: helping people get better.

This is your invitation.

Bring your ideas, your grit, and your care for people.
Join us and shape the future of care.
The Opportunity
Fullscript is looking for an AI Enablement Specialist to help Fullscripters use AI confidently, responsibly, and effectively in their day-to-day work.

You will join Team GSD, Fullscript's AI and automation enablement team. GSD helps departments improve how work gets done by combining practical AI education, workflow discovery, and scalable automation. This role will own the human side of that work: turning fast-moving AI capabilities and internal tools into clear, useful learning experiences that meet people where they are.
This is primarily a content, enablement, and adoption role. You will build the self-serve resources, interactive learning experiences, communications, and support models that help teams learn independently. You will also work with stakeholders to uncover workflow pain points, assess AI and automation opportunities, and translate what you learn into clear inputs for the GSD roadmap.
You will not be expected to build machine learning models or act as a full-time trainer. You should, however, be hands-on and credible with modern AI tools, curious about how people learn, and comfortable facilitating a live session or webinar when it is the best way to help a group move forward.
What you'll do

  • Own the creation of Fullscript’s AI training and development content, including practical guides, slide decks, blogs, videos, playbooks, templates, and role-based learning paths.

  • Build and continuously improve interactive, self-serve learning experiences that make Fullscript’s AI knowledge easy to find, understand, and apply independently.

  • Identify user groups, learning needs, and skill gaps across Fullscript, then tailor content to their workflows, business context, and level of AI fluency.

  • Stay current on AI tools, capabilities, use cases, and emerging trends, using that knowledge to keep Fullscript’s learning materials accurate, relevant, and practical.

  • Partner with AI Champions to shape departmental adoption roadmaps, equip them with reusable resources, and support the rollout and internal go-to-market of new AI tools.

  • Build strong relationships across the business, observe how teams work, and uncover operational pain points, knowledge gaps, and opportunities for AI or automation.

  • Gather requirements and frame opportunities by documenting the problem, users, current workflow, expected impact, data needs, feasibility, and risk, then translate those insights into clear recommendations for GSD roadmap planning.

  • Serve as a frontline enablement partner for GSD applications, turning recurring questions, adoption barriers, and user feedback into better content, product guidance, and roadmap inputs.

  • Measure and improve enablement through signals such as content engagement, tool usage, proficiency, support trends, time saved, and business impact.

  • Facilitate select workshops, webinars, office hours, or onboarding sessions, share useful practices across teams, and occasionally represent Fullscript at relevant industry events.

What you bring to the table

  • Experience in learning and development, technical enablement, digital learning, knowledge management, change enablement, developer education, or a related field.

  • Hands-on fluency with modern AI tools such as Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, or similar platforms, along with a practical understanding of what large language models can and cannot do.

  • Experience designing clear, engaging learning content for people with different roles, levels of technical knowledge, and ways of learning.

  • A track record of building self-serve resources or digital learning experiences that improved adoption, confidence, or performance.

  • Strong business analysis skills. You can uncover the real problem behind a request, map a workflow, gather requirements, and translate business needs into clear next steps for a technical team.

  • Excellent written communication and information design skills, with the judgment to make complex ideas simple without making them inaccurate.

  • Strong relationship-building skills and the ability to earn trust with both technical and non-technical stakeholders.

  • Strong project management and prioritization skills, with the ability to move several enablement initiatives forward without losing sight of quality or outcomes.

  • A practical, people-first approach to change. You understand that adoption depends on relevance, trust, clarity, and support, not simply access to a new tool.

  • Comfort facilitating a live learning session, webinar, or group discussion when needed.

Bonus if you have

  • Experience with low-code or no-code automation tools such as n8n, Zapier, or Make.

  • Experience creating interactive learning experiences or lightweight web applications using low-code, no-code, or AI-assisted development tools.

  • Familiarity with AI workflow concepts such as agents, connectors, model selection, evaluation, and human-in-the-loop review.

  • Experience launching internal tools or leading adoption and communication programs in a technology-driven organization.

  • Experience building or supporting a champions network, guild, cohort, or internal community of practice.

  • Familiarity with AI governance, data privacy, or enablement in healthcare or another regulated environment.

  • Experience speaking at industry events, facilitating communities, or creating external thought-leadership content.

What we can offer you

  • Remote-first flexibility to work where you work best, with Ottawa, Toronto, or Calgary preferred for this role.

  • Flexible PTO and competitive pay, because work-life balance matters

  • RRSP/401k match and competitive compensation packages to invest in your future

  • Premium benefits package with customizable coverage, paramedical services, and an HSA.

  • Fullscript discounts to save on high-quality wellness products

  • Continuous learning opportunities to grow your skills and career

Compensation range

The salary range for this role is between $80,000 and $90,000 (CAD). Fullscript shares salary ranges to support transparency and help candidates make informed decisions. The range shown reflects base salary only. The range shown reflects base salary only. Additional incentives, perks, and benefits may be available as part of Fullscript’s total rewards package.

Final compensation depends on experience, skills, and location. We review pay regularly to stay aligned with market data and internal equity. Benefits and total rewards may vary by region.

Why Fullscript

Great work happens when people feel supported, trusted, and inspired. At Fullscript, we stay curious and keep finding smarter ways to make care better. We grow together, take on new challenges, and focus on impact. We put people first, work as a team, and leave egos at the door.

What to Know Before You Apply

We’re grateful for the interest in joining Fullscript. To make sure your application reaches our hiring team, please apply directly through our careers page.

A quick note: Due to the high volume of applications, we’re not able to respond to phone or email inquiries about application status. If there’s a match, our team will reach out directly.

Fullscript is an equal opportunity employer committed to creating an inclusive workplace. Accommodations are available upon request at accommodations@fullscript.com.

All offers are contingent on successful background checks conducted in compliance with federal, state, and provincial laws.

We use AI tools to support parts of the hiring process, including screening and reviewing responses. Final hiring decisions are always made by people and follow all applicable privacy and employment laws in Canada and the U.S.

title: Executive Director, WA CIE
description:
Who is Comagine Health?

Comagine Health is a national, mission-driven, nonprofit organization that has engaged in health care quality consulting and quality improvement services for more than 50 years.

We are leaders in assisting front-line providers and engaging health care partners to improve care delivery and patient outcomes.

Our talented remote workforce spans the country and plays a vital role in our success. We go beyond merely providing a remote work option—we support and embrace it. You’ll have the opportunity to make an impact from anywhere in the U.S. while contributing to meaningful improvements in health care delivery and community health outcomes.

Position Overview

Comagine Health is seeking an experienced and strategic leader to serve as the Executive Director, Washington Community Information Exchange (CIE). This role serves as the senior leader and lead project manager for a multi-year partnership with the State of Washington to design, implement, and operationalize a statewide Community Information Exchange.

The Executive Director will provide strategic, operational, and financial oversight to support standardized data exchange, system interoperability, and scalable support for Community Care Hubs across Washington State. This leader will work closely with state agencies, community organizations, technology partners, and internal cross-functional teams to ensure successful delivery aligned with contractual obligations, statewide priorities, and Comagine Health’s mission and values.

Key Responsibilities

Operations Stewardship (80%)

  • Provide day-to-day leadership and management of the Washington CIE program
  • Ensure adequate staffing, regulatory compliance, and adherence to organizational and client policies
  • Lead cross-functional teams supporting implementation and operational delivery of the statewide CIE initiative
  • Drive achievement of key program objectives, including:
    • Standardization of Health-Related Social Needs (HRSN) service delivery data exchange
    • Interoperability between state, regional, and local technology systems
    • Scalability of Community Care Hub efforts across Washington State
  • Build and maintain strong partnerships with state agencies, providers, community organizations, and stakeholders

Financial Stewardship (10%)

  • Partner with the client, VP of Data Solutions, and organizational leaders to develop and manage project budgets
  • Provide oversight of Washington CIE program financials, including subcontractor budgets and resource allocation
  • Monitor financial performance and support long-term sustainability planning

Organizational Leadership (10%)

  • Foster collaboration and alignment across service lines and teams supporting the Washington CIE program
  • Support team development through communication, mentorship, and leadership engagement
  • Promote organizational values, mission, and culture throughout program operations

Qualifications

Required:

  • Master’s degree (MA/MS)
  • 10+ years of experience leading high-profile, large-scale engagements with Medicaid programs and/or state health agencies
  • 5+ years of leadership and people management experience
  • Demonstrated success managing complex, multi-stakeholder initiatives
  • Strong operational, strategic, and financial management capabilities
  • Excellent communication, relationship-building, and leadership skills

Preferred:

  • PMP, PgMP, or related project/program management certification
  • Experience with health information exchange, interoperability initiatives, or community-based care coordination models
  • Familiarity with Health-Related Social Needs (HRSN) programs and Community Care Hub models

Core Competencies

  • Advanced Communication
  • Advanced Interpersonal & Relationship Skills
  • Advanced Professionalism & Integrity
  • Advanced Work Ethic and Reliability
  • Advanced Results Orientation
  • Intermediate Technical Expertise
  • Advanced Project & Program Management

Work Environment

  • Primarily remote, home-based position
  • Requires reliable internet access and a distraction-free workspace
  • Frequent use of computers, phones, and virtual communication tools
